text:
**Findings**

High: [jobwatch/db.py](/work/jobwatch/db.py:70) lines 70-84 - terminal-state conflicts are last-write-wins, so an older terminal snapshot can overwrite a newer terminal record when ingested out of order.

High: [jobwatch/db.py](/work/jobwatch/db.py:74) lines 74-80 - records are treated as unchanged when only `state`, `end`, and `elapsed_sec` match, leaving corrected `alloc_cpus`, `gpus`, `partition`, `exit_code`, `submit`, or `start` data stale.

Medium: [jobwatch/db.py](/work/jobwatch/db.py:31) lines 31-41 - unknown states are ranked as terminal, so valid nonterminal states not in `_STATE_RANK` can block later lifecycle updates.

Medium: [jobwatch/reports.py](/work/jobwatch/reports.py:14) lines 14, 65, 83, 101, 115 - report windows rely on SQLite string comparison of ISO timestamps, which is incorrect for mixed timezone offsets and fragile if timezone-aware values enter the DB.

Medium: [jobwatch/parser.py](/work/jobwatch/parser.py:118) lines 118-126 - timestamps are normalized but not canonicalized to one timezone or one naive/aware convention, feeding the reporting comparison bug.

Low: [jobwatch/parser.py](/work/jobwatch/parser.py:137) lines 137-164 - required semantic fields like `User`, `Partition`, and `ExitCode` are not validated for emptiness, so bad rows can become misleading report data.

Low: [jobwatch/db.py](/work/jobwatch/db.py:52) lines 52-59 - `connect()` always creates/initializes the DB, so read-only report commands silently create an empty database on a wrong path.

Low: [jobwatch/db.py](/work/jobwatch/db.py:13) lines 13-27 - there is no schema versioning or migration path, which will make active development risky once columns or indexes change.

Low: [tests/test_ingest.py](/work/tests/test_ingest.py:40) lines 40-69 - ingest tests cover pending/running-to-terminal transitions but not terminal-vs-terminal ordering or metadata-only corrections.

Low: [tests/test_reports.py](/work/tests/test_reports.py:56) lines 56-66 - report tests cover naive ISO dates only, missing timezone-offset and mixed timestamp cases.

Tests run: `python -m pytest -q` passed, 61 tests. The warning was only pytest cache creation failing because `/work` is read-only for cache writes in this environment.

Overall score: **6.5/10**. The code is small, readable, and covered for intended examples, but the ingest path has real data-staleness/data-corruption risks. I would **not approve as-is** for a PR until the upsert semantics and timestamp handling are fixed.

Estimated rewrite/significant-change size: **120 lines** across `db.py`, `parser.py`, `reports.py`, and focused tests.

issues.description: Terminal-state conflicts are last-write-wins, so older terminal snapshots can overwrite newer terminal records.
Metadata-only corrections are marked unchanged and leave stale CPU/GPU/partition/exit-code data in the database.
Unknown states are ranked as terminal, which can block later updates from valid unlisted nonterminal states.
Report windows compare ISO timestamps as strings, which is wrong for mixed timezone offsets.
Parsed timestamps are not canonicalized to a single timezone/format before storage.
Required semantic fields such as user, partition, and exit code can be empty without row rejection.
Report commands silently create an empty database when given a wrong database path.
SQLite schema has no versioning or migration mechanism.
Ingest tests miss terminal-vs-terminal ordering and metadata-only correction cases.
Report tests miss timezone-offset and mixed timestamp comparison cases.
